source_images.alt_text: Eratosthenes measurement diagram showing Syene, Alexandria, Sun rays, verticals, and a 7.1 degree angle.
source_images.instructional_job: Two measurements—distance and angle—are connected by a geometric model.

source_images.alt_text: Lunar eclipse geometry diagram showing Earth shadow and Moon shadow taper.
source_images.instructional_job: A shadow can become measurable evidence about an object that is far away.

source_images.alt_text: Scale diagram of the Sun, Moon orbit, and Earth.
source_images.instructional_job: Scale matters when a model is used to reason about a physical system.

source_images.alt_text: Coin and Moon distance-ratio diagram showing similar triangles.
source_images.instructional_job: Ratios can turn a simple local measurement into a model of a distant object.

source_images.alt_text: Half-Moon geometry diagram showing a right triangle with Sun, Moon, and Earth.
source_images.instructional_job: A model links what can be measured to a quantity that cannot be measured directly.

source_images.alt_text: Sun-diameter measurement diagram using a pinhole image and a ratio.
source_images.instructional_job: A repeatable measurement can support a claim about a very large, distant object.

source_images.alt_text: A tablecloth is pulled quickly from beneath dishes.
source_images.instructional_job: The dishes tend to keep their original state of motion.

source_images.alt_text: A card is accelerated from under a coin above a glass.
source_images.instructional_job: The card changes motion first; the coin tends to maintain its state.

source_images.alt_text: A hammer moves downward and stops suddenly.
source_images.instructional_job: A sudden change in one part of a system highlights inertia.

source_images.alt_text: A massive ball hangs between upper and lower strings.
source_images.instructional_job: How quickly the force changes can matter because the mass resists a change in motion.

source_images.alt_text: Four scaffold panels showing changing rope tension and equilibrium.
source_images.instructional_job: Changing how a load is shared changes individual support forces while the total can remain balanced.

source_images.alt_text: A table supports a book and a compressed spring pushes upward.
source_images.instructional_job: A surface can exert an upward support force even when the supported object is motionless.

source_images.alt_text: A person stands on a scale with weight downward and support force upward.
source_images.instructional_job: A scale reads a support force, not the net force.

source_images.alt_text: Perpendicular vectors form a rectangle whose diagonal is the resultant.

source_images.alt_text: Equal perpendicular vectors form a square with a diagonal resultant.
source_images.instructional_job: Equal perpendicular components produce a diagonal resultant longer than either component.

source_images.alt_text: A 30-N vector and 40-N vector produce a 50-N resultant.
source_images.instructional_job: Vector addition must preserve both magnitude and direction.
